intervals.label: development of the advanced UCN source
intervals.note: Start is a lower bound: after the 2017 first UCN production at TRIUMF with a prototype source, development of the advanced source continued. The experiment's start and approval dates are not stated in a source consulted.
intervals.quote: Since then, development has continued on a new, advanced UCN source designed to deliver UCNs at world-leading intensity [3].

intervals.label: commissioning of the source, first UCN production
intervals.note: A record production run took place on 13 June 2025 (KURNS and TRIUMF news); the liquid-deuterium moderator was not yet installed, and no later status is published. A site-wide shutdown of the TRIUMF accelerators was announced for 2026 in the collaboration's outlook (not recorded as an interval).
intervals.quote: Substantial progress in 2024 allowed the collaboration to operate the complete source system, with the exception of the liquid deuterium cold moderator, resulting in the first production of UCNs.

name: TUCAN
notes: Conflict: arXiv:2507.05278 (v4, July 2026) says the first UCN production followed progress in 2024, while KURNS and TRIUMF report the 13 June 2025 run as the record-setting production; the commissioning interval starts at 2024 (approximate) and the June 2025 run is recorded in its note.
The TRIUMF cyclotron is not recorded as an accelerator in this atlas (no accelerator:triumf record); listed for the integrator.

physics_goals.quote: The TRIUMF Ultracold Advanced Neutron (TUCAN) collaboration has been developing a high-intensity ultracold neutron (UCN) source aimed at searching for the neutron electric dipole moment (EDM)
physics_goals.value: Search for the neutron electric dipole moment with a sensitivity goal of 1e-27 e cm using a high-intensity ultracold neutron source

summary.plain: A Canadian-led collaboration building a very intense source of ultracold neutrons at TRIUMF in Vancouver, to search for the neutron’s electric dipole moment with a target sensitivity of 10^-27 electron-charge centimetres. The source made its first ultracold neutrons in 2024-2025.
summary.technical: TUCAN (TRIUMF Ultracold Advanced Neutron): accelerator-driven superfluid-helium UCN source on a 520 MeV cyclotron proton beam (design 1.6 x 10^7 UCN/s with the liquid-deuterium moderator) feeding a neutron EDM spectrometer with goal 10^-27 e cm. First UCN production in 2024; record run 13 June 2025 without the LD2 moderator.
